evidence_rule: Pattern maturity must be supported by sanitized evidence, operating conditions, failure modes, and a stated portability gap. Single-company evidence cannot by itself establish portability.

patterns.name: Zero-context resumability
patterns.problem: Long-running work fails when continuation depends on conversation history or individual memory.
patterns.mechanism: Durable state + plan + runbook + zero-context handoff + exact next action.
conditions: The durable control plane is accessible to the successor.
The current task and exact next action are maintained after substantive work.
Live external sources are revalidated when they can change.
failure_modes: State files become stale or are not updated after work.
Critical context remains only in chat or a person's memory.
The handoff points to artifacts that are no longer authoritative.
patterns.counterexample_or_limit: Short-lived work that is completed in one session may not justify a full durability scaffold.
patterns.falsifier: A zero-context qualified successor repeatedly cannot determine the current task or safe next action from durable state alone.
patterns.portability_gap: Not yet validated in a materially different company.

patterns.name: Bounded execution and checkpointing
patterns.problem: Large tasks are vulnerable to interruption, connector limits, retries, and partial completion.
patterns.mechanism: Deterministic batches, validation, checkpoint after each substantive batch, explicit remaining queue.
conditions: The work can be partitioned into objectively identifiable units or batches.
Completion can be validated independently of the conversation that performed it.
Remaining work can be reconstructed deterministically.
failure_modes: Batch boundaries are arbitrary and cannot be reconciled to source inventory.
Partial writes are counted as complete without validation.
Checkpoints omit the exact next boundary.
patterns.counterexample_or_limit: Highly atomic tasks with no meaningful intermediate state may not benefit from batching.
patterns.falsifier: Interrupted work routinely requires repeating previously validated batches because completed units cannot be identified.
patterns.portability_gap: Needs multi-domain validation beyond research/data workflows.

patterns.name: Working plane / durable control plane separation
patterns.problem: Forcing collaboration artifacts and durable operating state into one system creates friction or conflicting truths.
patterns.mechanism: Keep collaborative work in its best-fit system while versioning normalized control state separately.
conditions: Authority for each information class is explicitly declared.
References between planes are durable enough to reconcile.
The control plane stores state and relationships rather than duplicating every working artifact.
failure_modes: Both planes become independently editable authorities for the same information.
The control plane drifts because working-plane changes are never checkpointed.
Teams are forced into the control plane for routine collaboration, creating adoption friction.
patterns.counterexample_or_limit: A very small project may legitimately use one system for both work and control if authority remains unambiguous.
patterns.falsifier: Separation increases reconciliation cost more than it reduces ambiguity because ownership and synchronization rules are unclear.
patterns.portability_gap: Needs validation with tool stacks other than GitHub + Google/SharePoint.

patterns.name: No-dual-canonical rule
patterns.problem: Two editable copies of the same information class create reconciliation debt and hidden divergence.
patterns.mechanism: Declare one authoritative source and explicit replicas/exports/cutover state.
conditions: The authoritative source is named per information class.
Replicas or exports have a declared generation/import path.
Transitions between authorities have explicit cutover rules.
failure_modes: Users edit both the source and its export.
Authority changes without a cutover checkpoint.
A stale replica is silently treated as current.
patterns.counterexample_or_limit: Multi-master systems can be valid when conflict resolution is intentionally engineered; this pattern targets unmanaged dual authority.
patterns.falsifier: Declared single authority does not reduce reconciliation incidents because operational users cannot access or trust it.

patterns.name: Live-source revalidation before crediting checkpoint state
patterns.problem: External source systems can change after a durable checkpoint, invalidating prior classifications.
patterns.mechanism: Verify current source commit/tree/state and reconcile differences before resuming.
conditions: The external source has a detectable version, timestamp, digest, or queryable state.
The prior checkpoint records what source state it used.
Material differences can be reconciled before new work proceeds.
failure_modes: Source versions are not recorded.
Revalidation checks only that the source exists, not whether relevant content changed.
A changed source invalidates prior work but the project continues without reconciliation.
patterns.counterexample_or_limit: Immutable source artifacts do not require repeated revalidation once their identity is proven.
patterns.falsifier: Revalidation repeatedly fails to detect changes that materially alter earlier classifications.
patterns.portability_gap: Needs validation with non-code source systems such as CRM/ERP/HRIS.

patterns.name: Target accountability versus current execution authority
patterns.problem: Future-state roles cannot authorize present-day transformation work when those roles do not yet exist.
patterns.mechanism: Represent target owner and current executor separately, with explicit delegation.
conditions: The organization is in transition or has ambiguous staffing relative to the target model.
Current authority can be identified independently of target design.
Tasks can record both future accountability and present execution.
failure_modes: Target role labels are treated as if they confer current authority.
Temporary executors silently become permanent owners.
No one records who may actually adopt decisions.
patterns.counterexample_or_limit: In a stable organization where current and target roles are identical, the distinction may add little value.
patterns.falsifier: Separating target and current authority increases ambiguity or delays decisions without preventing real governance errors.
patterns.portability_gap: Requires sustained operating use and external validation.

patterns.name: Organizational bootstrap layer
patterns.problem: A transformation can deadlock if the governance structure required to execute it is itself the thing being created.
patterns.mechanism: Narrow temporary stewardship that exists only to bootstrap current-state truth and transition toward target governance.
conditions: A real bootstrap deadlock exists.
A current sponsor can authorize narrow temporary stewardship.
The temporary mechanism has an exit/review condition.
failure_modes: Bootstrap authority becomes permanent by inertia.
Temporary stewards exceed the narrow mandate.
The target-state role model is imposed before current-state evidence is understood.
patterns.counterexample_or_limit: Organizations with already-functional governance may not need a bootstrap layer.
patterns.falsifier: The bootstrap layer creates more governance debt than it resolves or cannot be retired cleanly.
patterns.portability_gap: Designed and activated, but repeated execution and successful retirement are not yet proven.

patterns.name: AI role incubation before human stewardship
patterns.problem: A needed function may not yet have a clear human owner or mature job definition.
patterns.mechanism: Chartered AI role conversation builds/proposes the function while binding authority remains human; later transfer durable state to a human steward.
conditions: The function can be meaningfully advanced through research, design, inventory, drafting, or other non-binding work.
The AI role has a durable charter and startup/handoff package.
Binding authority remains explicitly separate.
A durable repository preserves continuity beyond the chat.
failure_modes: The role conversation is mistaken for a human executive.
AI proposals are silently treated as adopted decisions.
The function accumulates in private chat rather than durable state.
No human takeover path is defined.
patterns.counterexample_or_limit: Functions dominated by licensed professional judgment, physical operations, or immediate human authority may be poor candidates for AI incubation.
patterns.falsifier: The AI-incubated function cannot be safely handed to a human without substantial reconstruction or creates recurring authority confusion.
patterns.portability_gap: No completed AI-incubation to human-stewardship transfer yet.

patterns.name: Proposal/adoption state separation
patterns.problem: Consultants and AI can blur recommendation with authorization.
patterns.mechanism: Explicit draft/proposed/adopted/superseded states and adoption authority.
conditions: The organization distinguishes recommendation from binding decision.
Adoption authority can be named.
Artifacts can carry lifecycle status.
failure_modes: Proposed artifacts are operationalized before approval.
Adoption authority is vague or distributed informally.
Status labels exist but are ignored in practice.
patterns.counterexample_or_limit: Purely informational artifacts that have no binding consequence may not need adoption state.
patterns.falsifier: Explicit states fail to reduce unauthorized implementation or create excessive approval latency for low-risk work.

patterns.name: Dependency-aware process change
patterns.problem: Local process/product changes create untracked downstream consequences.
patterns.mechanism: Employee suggestion -> triage -> candidate impact map -> accountable decision -> linked implementation -> validation -> adoption.
conditions: Material managed objects and dependencies can be identified.
Impact discovery is separated from scope approval.
Accountable owners can accept, reject, or defer candidate impacts.
failure_modes: Dependency maps are treated as automatic implementation scope.
The graph becomes too stale or detailed to support useful decisions.
Cross-functional owners are not available to decide impacts.
patterns.counterexample_or_limit: Tiny local changes with no meaningful downstream dependencies may not require a formal impact lifecycle.
patterns.falsifier: The dependency model consistently misses material downstream effects or creates more coordination overhead than the avoided failures justify.
patterns.portability_gap: Dependency graph is not yet fully implemented or tested through a complete cross-functional change cycle.

patterns.name: Separate truth dimensions
patterns.problem: Organizations collapse different notions of truth into a single convenient status.
patterns.mechanism: Model independent truth dimensions and require evidence appropriate to each dimension.
conditions: The domain genuinely contains distinct truth questions.
Each dimension has materially different evidence or time sensitivity.
Users understand why the dimensions should not be collapsed.
failure_modes: Dimensions are created without decision value.
The model becomes too complex for operators to maintain.
One dimension is still used as a proxy for another in practice.
patterns.counterexample_or_limit: Simple domains with one stable notion of truth do not need multiple dimensions.
patterns.falsifier: Separating truth dimensions adds complexity without preventing erroneous conclusions or improving decisions.
patterns.portability_gap: General abstraction needs business-domain examples outside the original source domain.

patterns.name: Multi-environment working-plane topology
patterns.problem: Provider-level or singular-working-plane models can misclassify evidence and governance when an organization uses multiple clouds, tenants, environments, services, or locations.
patterns.mechanism: Assign stable environment identity across provider, tenant/account, environment, service, and location; assign information authority separately and govern material flows between environments.
conditions: The organization has material system or tenant boundaries worth distinguishing.
Environment identity can be established reliably enough for evidence and routing.
Information classes can be assigned authority independently from provider choice.
failure_modes: The topology is over-modeled for a simple organization.
Provider name is still used as a proxy for tenant/environment identity.
Environment inventory exists but authority and flows remain ambiguous.
patterns.counterexample_or_limit: A small organization with one unambiguous workspace may not need more than a simple Level-1 topology.
patterns.falsifier: The added environment distinctions do not prevent evidence mistakes, routing errors, or authority ambiguity and create more maintenance cost than decision value.
patterns.portability_gap: Needs use in at least one materially different multi-tenant or multi-provider organization.

patterns.name: Maturity-adaptive connected discovery
patterns.problem: Uniform discovery either wastes effort by interviewing mature organizations about already-documented work or misses operating reality in poorly documented organizations.
patterns.mechanism: Choose the least intrusive evidence-acquisition profile that can establish a trustworthy baseline: process corpus, corpus plus targeted validation, targeted connected read, or broader authorized connected read; preserve evidence state and read-only defaults.
conditions: Client access scope and environment identity can be governed.
Existing process/document maturity can be assessed.
Human validation remains available for consequential ambiguity.
failure_modes: Broad connector access is used by default without need.
Observed activity is mistaken for adopted process or authority.
Wrong-tenant search results enter the baseline.
A process corpus is trusted without testing currentness or provenance.
patterns.counterexample_or_limit: Clients with strong authoritative process repositories may need little or no connected discovery.
patterns.falsifier: Connected discovery does not reduce discovery cost/latency or increases false conclusions, privacy exposure, or validation burden.
patterns.portability_gap: Needs comparative discovery runs across organizations with materially different documentation maturity.

patterns.name: Semantic terminology crosswalk before renaming
patterns.problem: Teams can use different labels for similar concepts, causing integration errors when names are treated as proof of semantic equivalence.
patterns.mechanism: Crosswalk terms by definition, object boundary, lifecycle, authority, fields, and relationships; classify mappings as exact, partial, broader, narrower, or not equivalent before changing source terminology.
conditions: The terms refer to potentially overlapping managed concepts.
Source terminology can remain stable during analysis.
A deliberate shared-language decision can be made later if needed.
failure_modes: Synonyms are assumed exact without field/lifecycle comparison.
One team's vocabulary is overwritten before semantics are understood.
Crosswalks become permanent ambiguity without a decision owner.
patterns.counterexample_or_limit: Purely cosmetic vocabulary differences with no durable schema or workflow impact may not justify formal crosswalking.
patterns.falsifier: Semantic crosswalking does not reduce integration defects or produces more coordination overhead than direct terminology convergence.
patterns.portability_gap: Needs validation during a real multi-team or cross-organization integration.

patterns.name: Parallel methodology observation queue
patterns.problem: Reusable method insights discovered during client execution can be lost when the formal methodology cursor is busy with unrelated work.
patterns.mechanism: Capture sanitized Method Observations immediately in a durable queue, then triage and operationalize them later without automatically changing the active methodology task.
conditions: Client-private evidence can remain separated from sanitized public method notes.
A Method Steward or methodology-maintenance context can triage observations.
Observation state is distinct from adoption/pattern maturity.
failure_modes: Every observation interrupts the active methodology cursor.
The queue becomes an untriaged idea backlog.
Client-confidential details leak into the public method repo.
Captured observations are treated as adopted doctrine.
patterns.counterexample_or_limit: Trivial observations with no plausible reusable mechanism do not require registration.
patterns.falsifier: Repeated field insights are still lost, or the observation queue creates enough administrative burden to discourage capture.
patterns.portability_gap: Needs repeated client-to-method capture and triage cycles demonstrating lower insight loss without cursor disruption.
